title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Operational Guidance
author: Sofia Ramirez
summary: Operational guidance for Redwood Inference finance and legal teams covering annual budgeting and forecasting cadence, contract intake and approval, procurement procedures and vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition & billing policies for hosted and dedicated products.
content:
Overview:
This document consolidates operational guidance across four key areas: budgeting & forecasting, contracts & legal intake, procurement procedures, and revenue recognition (RevRec) and billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product, and business operations partners. Use this as a single-source reference for thresholds, owners, timelines, and templates.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood business units and product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, and Add-ons).
- Excludes employment & payroll policies (see People Ops handbook).

1) Budgeting & Forecasting (annual & rolling):
- Cadence:
  1. Annual budget cycle: kickoff in May, drafts by August, approval by Finance Leadership in October, Board submission in November.
  2. Rolling quarterly forecast (RDF): updated monthly with variance analysis and reforecast published within 5 business days of month-close.
- Ownership:
  - Finance: lead process owner (FP&A).
  - Product & Eng: provide headcount plans, feature roadmaps, and expected spend cadence.
  - Sales/GTM: provide ARR bookings, pipeline coverage, and contract changes.
- Inputs & templates:
  - Use the FP&A template (Drive: /sheets/budget-template-2026). Required inputs: headcount, G&A, cloud & GPU costs, committed Dedicated revenue, COGS split by service.
- Approval thresholds:
  - Up to $50k annual: Manager approval
  - $50k–$250k annual: Director approval + Finance review
  - > $250k annual: VP Finance approval + CFO notification
- Key controls:
  - Variance > 10% month-over-month requires a variance memo and mitigation plan.
  - All material contractual revenue (> $250k ARR or >12-month term) must be flagged to RevRec team at contract signature.

2) Contracts & Legal Intake:
- Intake flow (summary):
  1. Sales/Partnerships submits Contract Intake Form (Confluence link) + preliminary SOW/term sheet.
 2. Legal triages for standard vs. non-standard terms. Non-standard items are routed to Legal Counsel with a target initial response of 3 business days.
 3. Commercial review (Finance) verifies pricing, billing terms, and RevRec implications.
 4. Sign-off workflow: Legal -> Finance -> Sales -> Exec (if required by approval matrix).
- Standard vs Non-standard definitions:
  - Standard: Redwood Master Services Agreement (MSA) + published SOW templates, standard data/residency clauses, standard indemnity and liability caps (see template).
  - Non-standard: changes to liability caps, indemnities, data residency, or IP terms; discounts > 30%; multi-year exclusivity; > $500k ARR.
- Approval matrix (quick reference):
  - Commercial discounts up to 10%: Sales Director
  - 10%–30% or non-standard payment terms: VP Sales + Finance Director
  - > 30% discount or > $500k ARR or strategic exceptions: CFO + Legal Partner
- Required artifacts before signature:
  - Signed MSA/SOW, Contract Intake ID, SSO & KMS requirements (if applicable), Customer security questionnaire status, Billing rate card, RevRec classification (Annual/Subscription/Professional Services).

3) Procurement & Vendor Onboarding:
- Procurement steps:
  1. Raise P.O. request in procurement system with vendor info, SOW, and expected spend.
 2. Procurement validates vendor legal entity, tax ID, W-9/Foreign equivalent, insurance certs, and sanctions screening.
 3. Finance assigns GL codes and budget owner confirms availability.
 4. PO issued; supplier onboarding completed; invoices routed to AP with PO reference.
- Vendor risk classification & SLA:
  - Low risk: < $50k annual, standard SaaS, no access to PHI/PCI — onboarding SLA 5 business days.
  - Medium risk: $50k–$250k, limited data access — SLA 10 business days, require DPAs and security questionnaire.
  - High risk: > $250k or access to sensitive data (PHI/PCI/highly regulated) — legal & security review required, SLA 20 business days.
- Payment & invoice processing:
  - Standard net terms: Net 30. Early payment discounts require Finance approval.
  - Non-PO invoices must be routed to procurement for review; repeated supplier exceptions require Controller approval.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies (RevRec):
- Revenue models covered:
  - Consumption (Hosted API per-token/embedding): recognized as usage occurs (ratable within month). Deferred revenue calculated daily for prepaid credits.
  - Subscription (Dedicated / Reserved capacity): recognized on a straight-line basis over the contract term.
  - Professional services / Implementation: recognize based on milestones or % completion per SOC and SOW (documented in contract).
  - One-time licensing or reseller fees: evaluated at contract level for performance obligations; recognized when control transfers.
- Billing cadence & invoices:
  - Hosted customers billed monthly in arrears (usage) unless prepaid contract exists.
  - Dedicated & Private customers billed per contract terms (monthly/quarterly/annual).
  - All invoices must include Contract ID, PO (if provided), product SKU, usage summary, and billing contact.
- Contract changes & amendments:
  - Material changes affecting revenue recognition (term changes, pricing, scope) must be routed to RevRec lead before signature.
  - Upgrades/downgrades prorated at change date per customer agreement.
- Deferred revenue & recognition controls:
  - RevRec team maintains a deferred revenue schedule updated daily; monthly close includes validation by Finance Ops and Contract owner.
  - Journal entries for deferred revenue recognition require two approvers for amounts > $50k.

5) Roles & Ownership (single-line owners):
- FP&A Lead: owns budgeting cadence and templates.
- RevRec Lead (Accounting): owns recognition policy and deferred revenue schedule.
- Legal Counsel (Commercial): owns contract templates & triage.
- Procurement Manager: owns vendor onboarding and PO issuance.
- Sales Operations: owns Contract Intake Form and Salesforce contract records.

6) Templates & Artifacts (links):
- Budget template (Drive): /sheets/budget-template-2026
- Contract Intake Form (Confluence): /confluence/forms/contract-intake
- PO request form (Procurement Portal): /procure/requests
- RevRec checklist & journal entry template (Drive): /sheets/revrec-journal-template

Appendix A — Approval Threshold Table:
| Type                         | Threshold                  | Approver(s)                           | Notes |
|------------------------------|---------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------|
| Budget line item              | <= $50k                   | Manager                                |       |
| Budget line item              | $50k - $250k              | Director + Finance review              |       |
| New vendor onboarding         | < $50k annual             | Procurement Manager                     | Low risk only |
| New vendor onboarding         | $50k - $250k              | Procurement + Security review          | Medium risk |
| Commercial discounts          | <= 10%                   | Sales Director                          |       |
| Commercial discounts          | 10% - 30%                | VP Sales + Finance Director            |       |
| Contract exceptions           | > $500k ARR              | CFO + Legal Partner                    | Strategic exceptions |
